## Context

Gkeyll has no formatting standard today: no `.clang-format`, no `.editorconfig`, no CI lint job, no pre-commit hooks. Goal: adopt a Linux-kernel-flavored style with 2-space indentation for all C/C++/CUDA source, excluding `*/ker/*` (auto-generated DG kernel code — ~63% of all C/C++ files in the repo, machine-generated by a Maxima-based code generator and never hand-edited, per the existing `gkeyll_guide` skill). The style must be enforced consistently for both human contributors and coding agents, going forward, without relying on people remembering to run a formatter.

Decisions already made with the user:
- Ignore `origin/uncrustify`; start fresh.
- Include `.cu`/`.cuh` files in the formatting scope (clang-format handles CUDA reasonably well in modern versions) — spot-check kernel-launch syntax before committing to the repo-wide reformat.
- Human enforcement: a `pre-commit` hook that **auto-fixes** formatting at commit time (not just check-and-block).
- Agent enforcement: a **new, dedicated** SKILL file (not folded into `gkeyll_guide`) documenting the style so agents are aware of it and can run it themselves; the same pre-commit/CI machinery is the actual gate regardless of who authored the change.

## Scope

- Format: `.c`, `.h`, `.cpp`, `.hpp`, `.cu`, `.cuh` under `core/`, `moments/`, `vlasov/`, `gyrokinetic/`, `pkpm/`, `gkeyll/` (the `apps/`, `creg/`, `unit/`, `zero/`, `luareg/`, `amr*/`, `proofs/` subdirs, plus `gkeyll/gkeyll.c` and the small amount of glue C under `gkeyll/lua/Comm`, `gkeyll/lua/Tool`).
- Exclude: any path matching `*/ker/*` (auto-generated kernels) and `build/` (already gitignored, generated). Vendored Lua libs under `gkeyll/lua/` are Lua, not C, so naturally out of scope.

Base on clang-format's built-in `Linux` style (K&R-ish brace placement matching what the codebase already does informally) and override indentation to 2 spaces:

```yaml

IndentWidth: 2
TabWidth: 2
UseTab: Never
ContinuationIndentWidth: 4
ColumnLimit: 100

- Add a small helper script (e.g. `dev/format-all.sh`) that lists tracked files under the scoped directories, excludes `*/ker/*`, and runs `clang-format -i` on them.

# Roll out clang-format (Linux kernel style, 2-space indent) across gkeyll

## Context

Gkeyll has no formatting standard today: no `.clang-format`, no `.editorconfig`, no CI lint job, no pre-commit hooks. There was a prior, unfinished attempt on the unmerged `origin/uncrustify` branch (uncrustify-based, excludes `.cu` files entirely due to CUDA `<<<...>>>` mangling) — per user decision, that branch is stale and will be ignored; this plan builds a clang-format-based setup from scratch instead.

Goal: adopt a Linux-kernel-flavored style with 2-space indentation for all C/C++/CUDA source, excluding `*/ker/*` (auto-generated DG kernel code — ~63% of all C/C++ files in the repo, machine-generated by a Maxima-based code generator and never hand-edited, per the existing `gkeyll_guide` skill). The style must be enforced consistently for both human contributors and coding agents, going forward, without relying on people remembering to run a formatter.

Decisions already made with the user:
- Ignore `origin/uncrustify`; start fresh.
- Include `.cu`/`.cuh` files in the formatting scope (clang-format handles CUDA reasonably well in modern versions) — spot-check kernel-launch syntax before committing to the repo-wide reformat.
- Human enforcement: a `pre-commit` hook that **auto-fixes** formatting at commit time (not just check-and-block).
- Agent enforcement: a **new, dedicated** SKILL file (not folded into `gkeyll_guide`) documenting the style so agents are aware of it and can run it themselves; the same pre-commit/CI machinery is the actual gate regardless of who authored the change.

## Scope

- Format: `.c`, `.h`, `.cpp`, `.hpp`, `.cu`, `.cuh` under `core/`, `moments/`, `vlasov/`, `gyrokinetic/`, `pkpm/`, `gkeyll/` (the `apps/`, `creg/`, `unit/`, `zero/`, `luareg/`, `amr*/`, `proofs/` subdirs, plus `gkeyll/gkeyll.c` and the small amount of glue C under `gkeyll/lua/Comm`, `gkeyll/lua/Tool`).
- Exclude: any path matching `*/ker/*` (auto-generated kernels) and `build/` (already gitignored, generated). Vendored Lua libs under `gkeyll/lua/` are Lua, not C, so naturally out of scope.
- ~1600 files will actually be reformatted (vs. ~4359 total C/C++ files in the repo, most of which are `ker/`).

## Implementation

### 1. `.clang-format` at repo root
Base on clang-format's built-in `Linux` style (K&R-ish brace placement matching what the codebase already does informally) and override indentation to 2 spaces:

```yaml
BasedOnStyle: Linux
IndentWidth: 2
TabWidth: 2
UseTab: Never
ContinuationIndentWidth: 4
ColumnLimit: 100
```

Pin a specific clang-format **version** (not just the config) in the tooling below — output differs across versions, and `.cuh`/`.cu` language-detection has changed across releases. Use a recent stable release (e.g. 18.x).

During initial rollout, run this config over a representative sample (plain C, a `.cpp`, and a `.cu` file with a `<<<...>>>` kernel launch) and eyeball the diff before reformatting the whole tree — adjust knobs like `PointerAlignment`, `IndentCaseLabels`, `AlignConsecutiveAssignments` if the default `Linux` choices look wrong for this codebase's existing conventions.

### 2. One-time repo-wide reformat
- Add a small helper script (e.g. `dev/format-all.sh`) that lists tracked files under the scoped directories, excludes `*/ker/*`, and runs `clang-format -i` on them.
- Run it once, review the diff (spot-check CUDA files especially), and commit as a single, isolated commit (e.g. "Apply clang-format formatting repo-wide").
- Add that commit's SHA to a new `.git-blame-ignore-revs` file at repo root, and document `git config blame.ignoreRevsFile .git-blame-ignore-revs` in the contributing docs, so `git blame` keeps working across the reformat.

### 3. Enforcement for humans: `pre-commit`
This repo doesn't use `pre-commit` yet — introduce it:
- Add `.pre-commit-config.yaml` at repo root using `pre-commit/mirrors-clang-format` pinned to the same clang-format version as above, with:
  - `files:` regex matching `\.(c|h|cpp|hpp|cu|cuh)$`
  - `exclude:` regex matching `(^|/)ker/`
  - default mirror behavior reformats in place (`-i`), which satisfies "auto-fix on commit."
- Document setup (one-time `pip install pre-commit && pre-commit install`) in a short new `CONTRIBUTING.md` section, alongside the style rationale and the `ker/` exclusion reason.

### 4. Enforcement in CI
- Add a new job (either a new `.github/workflows/format-check.yml` or a step appended to the existing `mac_build.yml`) that runs `pre-commit run --all-files` via the `pre-commit/action` GitHub Action (or manually installs and runs `pre-commit`).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run clang-format over every in-scope C/C++/CUDA file in the repo.
#
# In scope: tracked *.c/*.h/*.cpp/*.hpp/*.cu/*.cuh files, excluding anything
# under a */ker/* directory (auto-generated DG kernel code -- see
# .agents/skills/code_style/SKILL.md).
#
# Usage:
#   dev/format-all.sh          # reformat all in-scope files in place
#   dev/format-all.sh --check  # fail (exit 1) if any in-scope file is not formatted
set -euo pipefail

repo_root=$(git -C "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cd "$repo_root"

mode=${1:-}

mapfile -d '' files < <(
  git ls-files -z -- '*.c' '*.h' '*.cpp' '*.hpp' '*.cu' '*.cuh' \
    | grep -zv '/ker/'
)

if [[ "$mode" == "--check" ]]; then
  status=0
  for f in "${files[@]}"; do
    if ! clang-format --dry-run --Werror "$f" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "not formatted: $f"
      status=1
    fi
  done
  exit "$status"
else
  printf '%s\0' "${files[@]}" | xargs -0 clang-format -i
  echo "Formatted ${#files[@]} files."
fi
